original_question: Let S be a semigroup and let X be any set. A semigroup conjugacy relation on S is partition-covering if, for every partition of X, one can put a semigroup structure on X whose conjugacy classes are exactly the blocks of that partition. For the standard semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o, defined by a ∼o b when there exist g,h in S with ag = gb and bh = ha; ∼p, defined by a ∼p b when there exist u,v in S with a = uv and b = vu; and ∼tr, the epigroup relation defined using idempotent powers a^ω and b^ω together with elements g,h satisfying ghg = g, hgh = h, hg = a^ω, gh = b^ω, and ga^(ω+1)h = b^(ω+1), must every partition arise as the set of conjugacy classes of some semigroup?
target_in_paper: Section 3, 'Partition-Covering Problem'—specifically the partition-covering question introduced in Section 1 and resolved (in strengthened form) by Theorem 3.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s main 'partition-covering' theme, correctly asks for realizability of arbitrary set partitions as conjugacy classes, and correctly names three relations treated in the paper: ∼o, ∼p, and ∼tr. The defining equations you give for ∼p and for the trace relation ∼tr match the paper’s setup in substance, and the universal quantifier over all partitions is aligned with the paper’s intent.
missing_details: Partition-covering is a property of a conjugacy notion across all semigroups (or epigroups where relevant), not of one fixed semigroup S. The paper phrases it as: for every set X and every partition of X, there exists a suitable algebraic structure on the underlying set X whose conjugacy classes are exactly the blocks.
The relation ∼tr is defined only for epigroups, so in the ∼tr case the realizing structure must be an epigroup on X, not just an arbitrary semigroup.
The notation a^ω in the definition of ∼tr refers to the idempotent power of a in an epigroup; that ambient assumption should be stated explicitly.
Your draft does not match the paper’s exact historical open-problem framing: Section 3 says the cited Problem 6.10 asks about ∼o, ∼c, and ∼tr, whereas your draft replaces ∼c with ∼p.
If one wants the exact theorem-level formulation proved in this paper, Theorem 3.3 is broader than your draft: it proves partition-covering for ∼o, ∼c, ∼n, ∼p, ∼p*, and ∼tr.
refined_question: For each of the semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o and ∼p on arbitrary semigroups, and the trace conjugacy ∼tr on epigroups—where a ∼o b means there exist g,h with ag = gb and bh = ha, a ∼p b means there exist u,v with a = uv and b = vu, and for an epigroup a ∼tr b means that, writing a^ω and b^ω for the idempotent powers, there exist g,h such that ghg = g, hgh = h, hg = a^ω, gh = b^ω, and ga^(ω+1)h = b^(ω+1)—is the relation partition-covering in the sense that for every set X and every partition P of X, there exists a semigroup structure on the underlying set X (and, in the ∼tr case, an epigroup structure on X) whose conjugacy classes with respect to the chosen relation are exactly the blocks of P?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s 'Problem One' material: the abstract and Section 1 define partition-covering, and Section 3 proves partition-covering results. The sharp paper-faithful correction is to treat partition-covering as a property of the conjugacy notion itself, quantified over every set and every partition, and to make explicit that ∼tr is only defined for epigroups via idempotent powers a^ω. I kept your focus on ∼o, ∼p, and ∼tr instead of broadening the question to all six relations in Theorem 3.3, but I note in the missing details that the paper’s exact cited open problem was about ∼o, ∼c, and ∼tr, while the paper’s theorem strengthens this to six conjugacies.
